extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, businesses and institutions applying for UKRI funding (including Innovate UK applicants and higher education institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes how UKRI assesses research and innovation funding applications (applicant-led and targeted modes), including expert review, panel moderation, prioritisation into tiers, and specific approaches for Innovate UK and Research England allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment focus: excellence (and impact where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application for funding will be assessed by experts for excellence and, where applicable, impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is against published assessment criteria. Whether impact is considered depends on the opportunity ('where applicable').

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment mode: applicant-led vs targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of assessment will depend on the funding mode applied to the opportunity: applicant-led mode uses expert review and moderating panels; targeted mode uses assessment panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full details of the assessment process used will be included in each funding opportunity; applicants should check the specific opportunity for which mode and process apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert review
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an expert review stage, we appoint experts from the UK and overseas with recognised expertise in the relevant areas of research and innovation to review applications against published assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This part of the process does not typically benchmark the assessment against other applications to the funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderating panel inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the assessment process includes an expert review stage, a moderating panel is used to complete the assessment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members will assess and score based on the information provided in the application, reviews received from experts, and applicant response to the reviewer comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment panel: independent, evidence-based judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment panels are used when there is no expert review stage. Panel members assess the application independently against the assessment criteria, making an evidence-based judgement and scoring the application based on their expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel will discuss and agree a consensus score using the scoring table. The score agreed by the panel and based on how well the assessment criteria have been met will be used to group applications into tiers or to rank them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring outcome: grouping into tiers or ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: The score agreed by the panel and based on how well the assessment criteria have been met will be used to group applications into tiers. Where tiers are not practical, applications will be ranked in priority for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After scoring, applications are prioritised using a tiered approach or, if not practical, a fully ranked list based on overall score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier definitions (decision-making)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tiered approach is used, applications are assigned to one of three tiers: Tier 1, the highest quality, prioritised for funding; Tier 2, highly competitive, selected by assessment tools and dependent on remaining budget; Tier 3, not competitive enough to be considered for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation to tiers determines prioritisation for funding; where tiers are not practical, ranking by score determines funding order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritisation tools: banding, randomised and strategic allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: We will use a tiered approach to make decisions, using assessment tools such as banding, randomised and strategic allocation so that the aims of the opportunity are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools are used to select from within tiers (particularly Tier 2) to meet opportunity aims and budget constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The feedback provided to applicants will be dependent on the assessment approach used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically, applications submitted to applicant-led opportunities will receive their expert reviewer comments as feedback. Applications discussed at an assessment panel, or an interview panel, will receive feedback provided by the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment sensitivity and support for diverse research
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is designed to be sensitive to different needs and cultures in the academic community, reflecting the need to support different types of research and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels should take account of different research types and cultural/need-based considerations when making judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovate UK: technical and commercial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovate UK applications are reviewed by independent expert assessors from business and academia in the relevant areas of technical and commercial expertise. The Innovate UK funders panel makes the final assessment on which projects to fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment for Innovate UK emphasises both technical merit and commercial feasibility/expertise; final funding decisions are made by the funders panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio approach (Innovate UK funding allocations)
rubrics_metrics.description: We may also make funding allocations based on a portfolio approach spread across scope areas, categories of research and development, project durations, project costs, including demonstrating value for money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach ensures funds are allocated across strategic areas of the competition; all successful applications must meet the required quality threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality threshold requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All successful applications must meet the required quality threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where portfolio or other allocation approaches are used, applications must first reach a minimum quality standard to be eligible for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research England allocation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Research England allocates most of its funding to eligible higher education institutions based on the Research Excellence Framework assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allocation formula includes number of research staff, amount and quality of research undertaken, and amount of research and knowledge exchange income received. Performance is assessed periodically through the REF.
